Shanghai Municipal Council.

April 28th 1916

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / JUNCTA IN UNO / SHANGHAI）
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH)

Sir,
The majority of the people in Wusieh are in sympathy with the rebels, but, whatever happens, they do not want any fighting in their own city. Trouble in Wusieh at the present time or during the next two months would mean huge financial losses to the merchants for the silk season there will be soon at its height. During the fighting outside Wusieh on 23rd inst, several of the wives of officials and merchants took refuge in the foreign mission buildings and still remain there.

Everything is quiet in Soochow. The streets are patrolled by armed troops, police and Volunteers. No trouble has occurred but all kinds of wild rumours are rife. The people and a good percentage of the military are in sympathy with the Republicans. Were either Nanking or Shanghai to declare independence, Soochow would soon follow their example, but until either of these things happen, Soochow will most likely remain loyal to the Central Government. There are about 2,000 infantry, 100 cavalry, 100 artillery men and 100 engineers at Soochow, besides a local Volunteer Corps of about 750 men. The latter body is said to be very much pro-rebel. The Soochow Authorities seem to be taking great precautions. All Chinese letters leaving the town are censored. The baggage of all persons arriving is searched. Soldiers and police visit the Chinese lodging houses nightly and interview all new arrivals.

On 21st inst about two hundred revolutionaries under a man named Ho Kya Loh 何家祿 an ex-Captain of the Chinese navy who was in Soochow during the 2nd revolution; captured Wukiang 吳江 a small town about 36 li from Soochow where there were no soldiers and only about forty policemen. The capture was effected without much bloodshed. On the 23rd inst 500 infantry, 150 water police and thirty cavalrymen went from Soochow to attack the rebels. They encountered the latter outside the village. Desultory fighting continued during the day during which about twenty men were wounded on each side and a few

1916年4月28日

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / JUNCTA IN UNO / SHANGHAI）
警务处，
（侦探股）

先生：

吴县（Wusieh）的大多数民众同情叛军，但无论发生何种情况，他们都不希望在自己的城市内发生战斗。目前或未来两个月内，吴县若发生动乱，将给商人带来巨大的经济损失，因为当地的丝绸旺季即将到来。在23日吴县外围的战斗中，数名官员和商人的眷属避难于外国传教士的建筑物内，至今仍滞留在那里。

苏州（Soochow）一切平静。街道由武装部队、警察及万国商团巡逻。虽未发生骚乱，但各种荒诞谣言盛行。民众以及相当比例的军人同情共和派。一旦南京或上海宣布独立，苏州很快就会效仿；但在此之前，苏州很可能仍忠于中央政府。苏州驻有步兵约2,000人、骑兵100人、炮兵100人及工兵100人，此外还有一支约750人的地方万国商团。据称，后者非常倾向于支持叛军。苏州当局似乎正在采取严密的预防措施。所有离开该城的中文信件均受审查。所有抵达人员的行李均受搜查。士兵和警察每晚走访华人客栈，盘问所有新到者。

本月21日，约两百名革命党人在一名叫何家祿（Ho Kya Loh）的人率领下，攻占了吴江（Wukiang）。何家祿系前中国海军上尉，曾在二次革命期间身处苏州。吴江是距苏州约36里的一座小镇，当时那里没有驻军，仅有约四十名警察。此次占领未造成大量流血。本月23日，500名步兵、150名水警和30名骑兵从苏州出发进攻叛军。他们在村外与叛军遭遇。当天断断续续的战斗中，双方各有约二十人受伤，另有数人

were killed. The rebels fled under cover of darkness,
and the Soochow troops took possession of the village
on the following day. This band of rebels seems to have
dispersed for its exact whereabouts is not at present
known. It is said that some of the band came from
Shanghai and that others were pirates from the Tahu Lake.

Kiangyin was re-taken by Government troops on the
evening of 26th inst. It is stated that when they
entered the forts they only found about fifty men, the
others having fled because their ammunition had run short.
It appears Nyeu Tih Sung 钮铁生 and other rebel leaders
in Shanghai had promised to send ammunition, but failed
to do so. Nyeu is reported to have returned to Shanghai.
His followers are beginning to lose faith in him.
Woo Kya Loh 何家禄 who led the rebels at Wu Kiang 吴江 has
also returned to Shanghai and is staying with Nyeu
in the western part of Frenchtown.

It is reported that the rebels here are endeavouring
to arrange to hold meetings in Chang Su Ho's garden
on 29th and 30th instant. The meeting will be ostensibly
for the purpose of discussing the general situation but
their real purpose will be an attempt to secure the
support of the public for the rebel cause.
It is said that the rebels had planned a rising
at a place in Pootung and that their intention became
known to the Catholic priest of the district who applied
to the authorities for protection.
Tuan Jieu Sai 段祺瑞 has telegraphed to General
Yang instructing him to maintain peace in Shanghai and
not to interfere with Chekiang in the meantime.

Your Obedient Servant,
（签名）
Chief Detective Inspector.
（签名）
Captain Superintendent of Police.

警务处，
（侦探股）
(2)

阵亡。叛军在夜色掩护下逃窜，
苏州部队于次日占领了该村。这股叛军似乎已
溃散，其确切下落目前尚不清楚。据说该股匪徒中部分来自
上海，另一些则是太湖（Tahu Lake）的海盗。

江阴（Kiangyin）已于本月26日晚被政府军收复。据称，政府军
进入炮台时，仅发现约五十人，其余人员因弹药耗尽而
逃离。看来，上海的叛军首领钮铁生（Nyeu Tih Sung）等人曾承诺
运送弹药，但未能兑现。据报道，钮铁生已返回上海。
他的追随者开始对他失去信心。率领叛军攻打吴江（Wu Kiang）的
何家祿（Woo Kya Loh）也已返回上海，正与钮铁生一同
居住在法租界（Frenchtown）西部。

据报道，此地的叛军正试图安排于本月29日和30日
在张叔和（Chang Su Ho）的花园举行集会。集会表面上
是为了讨论总体局势，但其真实目的是企图争取公众
对叛军事业的支持。
据说叛军曾计划在浦东（Pootung）某地发动起义，但其意图
被该地区的一位天主教神父获悉，该神父已向当局
请求保护。
段祺瑞（Tuan Jieu Sai）已致电杨将军，指示他维持上海
的和平，同时不得干涉浙江事务。

您顺从的仆人，
（签名）
总探长。
（签名）
警务处处长。
批注于 M.L Apt. 28
副本已送交 S.V.C.
